body:
Alice and Bob are tired of playing with messages and proving things which the lazy cryptographers should be doing on their own. So they've decided to take the day off, and have come to the beach. Alice soon spots a dirty glass bottle floating in the water, and they find an ancient parchment inside it. On it, is drawn an undirected graph! As luck would have it, they find some colored clam shells lying around. There are red, blue and green ones. And as usual, Alice devises some devious game and challenges Bob to play it.

She marks the vertices as V1, V2, .., VN. She then places some clams on each of the vertices. There are R1 red clams on V1, R2 red clams on V2, .., RN red clams on VN. Similarly there are Bi blue clams on Vi, for every i, and Gi green clams on Vi for every i. She tells Bob that he has to take every single clam and do one of two things: Suppose the clam was on Vi originally. He should either leave it at Vi itself. Or move it along an edge incident on Vi, and place it on a neighbouring vertex. He can do this atmost once, for every clam.

Suppose he does so for every clam, and finally ends up with a configuration, where there are R1' red clams on V1, R2' red clams on V2, .., RN' red clams on VN. Similarly there are Bi' blue clams on Vi, for every i, and Gi' green clams on Vi for every i.

She then gives him a sequence of numbers: T1, T2, .., TN, and tells him that, at the end, Vi should have a total of exactly Ti clams. That is, Ri' + Bi' + Gi' should be equal to Ti.

She gives him another sequence of numbers: MinG1, MinG2, .., MinGN, and tells him that there should be at least MinGi green clams on Vi. ie. Gi' should be greater than or equal to MinGi.

She also gives him an integer K, and Bob has to ensure that the total number of red clams which end up on even-indexed vertices is at least K. V2i is an even-indexed vertex, for all i. V2i+1 is an odd-indexed vertex, for all i. That is, R2' + R4' + .. + R2i' + .. should be greater than or equal to K.

Bob is lazy as usual and doesn't want to spend time trying, unless he knows for sure that this is achievable. Help him by figuring it out for him. Output 1 if he can satisfy all of Alice's conditions. Output 0 otherwise.

Input

The first line of input contains an integer T denoting the number of test cases. The description of T test cases follows.

The first line contains two integers N and M, denoting the number of vertices, and number of edges in the graph, respectively.

The next M lines contain two integers each, separated by single spaces: i j, denoting that there is an edge between Vi and Vj. It is guaranteed that there is atmost 1 edge between any two vertices, and there is no edge which connects a vertex to itself.

The next line contain N integers, separated by single spaces: R1, R2, .., RN, denoting the number of red clams in each vertex originally.

The next line contain N integers, separated by single spaces: B1, B2, .., BN, denoting the number of blue clams in each vertex originally.

The next line contain N integers, separated by single spaces: G1, G2, .., GN, denoting the number of green clams in each vertex originally.

The next line contain N integers, separated by single spaces: T1, T2, .., TN, denoting the total number of clams that Alice wants Bob to place in each vertex finally.

The next line contain N integers, separated by single spaces: MinG1, MinG2, .., MinGN, denoting the minimum number of green clams that Alice wants Bob to place in each vertex finally.

The last line contains a single integer K, denoting the minimum number of red clams that Alice wants Bob to place in even-indexed vertices finally.

Output

Output a single line for each testcase, containing the answer, which should be a 0 or a 1.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ T ≤ 3
  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 100
  • 0 ≤ M ≤ 1000
  • 0 ≤ Ri, Bi, Gi ≤ 100
  • 0 ≤ Ti, MinGi, K ≤ 3*104

Example

Input:
1
4 4
1 2
2 3
3 1
4 3
2 0 1 2
0 1 1 2
1 3 1 3
1 3 8 5
0 0 7 0
5

Output:
1

Explanation

Bob does these actions:
  • Moves both the red clams from V1 to V2.
  • Moves all the three green clams from V2 to V3.
  • Moves the red clam from V3 to V4.
  • Moves all the three green clams from V4 to V3.

    • Once these are done, we see that all of Alice's conditions are met:

  • The total number of clams in V1, V2, .. V4 is (1, 3, 8, 5). We see that each element here is exactly equal to the corresponding element in T1, T2, .., T4, which is (1, 3, 8, 5).
  • The number of green clams in V1, V2, .. V4 is (1, 0, 7, 0). We see that each element here is greater than or equal to the corresponding element in MinG1, MinG2, .., MinG4, which is (0, 0, 7, 0).
  • There are 2 red clams in V2 and 3 red clams in V4. Hence, there are at least K=5 red clams in even-indexed vertices.

    • Hence the answer is 1.
    All submissions for this problem are available.
